questions.question: What happens to the decomposition rate when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** It is slower.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The following **variables influence **the rate of decomposition:

 
 
• 
 **Chemical **make-up of detritus,
 
 
• 
 **pH**,
 
 
• 
 **Temperature**,
 
 
• 
 **Moisture, **and
 
 
• 
 **Aeration **of the **soil**.
 
 
 
 
• 
 Decomposition **proceeds **more **quickly **when the soil is **rich **in **nitrogen**.
 
 
• 
 The rate of decomposition is **accelerated **by the presence of **water**-**soluble carbohydrates**.
 
 
• 
 The degradation process is **slowed **down by the presence of big complex polymers in the debris, like** lignin and chitin.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The **breakdown** of **dead organic **matter into more **fundamental organic **or **inorganic **components including carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars, and mineral salts is known as decomposition, also referred to as rot.
 
• The process, which is a part of the **nutrient cycle**, is essential for recycling the scant material that occupies space in the biosphere.
 
• When a living organism passes away, the body begins to **decompose**.
 
• **Animals **like worms also contribute to the **breakdown **of the **chemical molecules**.
 
• Organisms that carry out this process are known as **decomposers **or **detritivores**.

questions.question: ______ is an environmental policy under which producers are given a significant responsibility - financial and/or physical - for the treatment or disposal of products that are no longer useful to the consumer.
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Environmental policy:**

__
 
• It is a kind of **measure** or unit that is taken by a** different kind of organization** like government and private regarding a **different kind of effect of human activities on the environment.**
 
• This is majorly created for the **prevention of human-made effects on the ecosystem.**
 
• Different kinds of environmental policies are ecosystem management, waste management, natural resources protection, and biodiversity conservation.

**Explanation:**__

**Extended Producer Responsibility:**

__
 
• This policy's concept was first introduced by the **Swedish Ministry of Environment in 1990.**
 
• Today's world is facing an increasing amount of waste and its effect on the environment.
 
• Different governments around the world are trying to control this problem with the post-consumer phase by environmental policy.
 
• The correct answer is Extended Producer Responsibility.
 
• EPR refers to an environmental policy that sees producers responsible for the safe disposal of their products.
 
• It is the responsibility, that the waste generated during the production processes should be taken care of in a proper way, from an environmental and resource-saving point of view.
 
• Before the manufacturing of a product is commenced it should be known how the waste, which is a result of the production process, should be treated, as well as how the product should be taken care of when discarded.
 
• The ultimate goal of EPR is sustainable development through environmentally responsible product development and product recovery.
 
• Its main objective is to divert and reduce waste.
 
• Here **producers** of a product **take full responsibility for their products' whole lifecycle **including recycling, reuse, final disposal, and packaging.

**Thus, extended producer responsibility is an environmental policy under which producers are given a significant responsibility - financial and/or physical - for the treatment or disposal of products that are no longer useful to the consumer.**__

questions.question: Which of the following steps is NOT involved in a Water Cycle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The hydration** step is NOT involved in a Water Cycle.
 
• **Hydration** involves replenishing the **body fluids** that are lost through sweating, exhaling, and waste elimination.
 
• Typically, the body loses and requires to replacement of approximately 2-3 quarts of water each day.
 
• Fortunately, many of the foods we consume are predominantly made up of water. Examples of such foods include leafy greens, as well as most fruits and vegetables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The water cycle,** also referred to as the hydrologic cycle or hydrological cycle, illustrates the perpetual movement of water across the Earth's surface, in the atmosphere, and beneath it.
 
• Throughout this cycle, water undergoes transitions between different states, while the total quantity of water particles remains constant.
 
• These state changes encompass processes such as evaporation, melting, freezing, sublimation, condensation, and deposition, all of which necessitate the input or release of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation** represents the transformation of water vapor in the atmosphere into liquid water, contrasting with the process of evaporation. This step is pivotal in the water cycle as it leads to the formation of clouds.
 
• Above 0 degrees Celsius, water vapor condenses into water droplets. However, this condensation doesn't occur spontaneously; it relies on the presence of dust or other impurities. Water vapor adheres to the surface of these particles, eventually forming droplets. As these droplets coalesce, they precipitate out of clouds and onto the ground below, a phenomenon known as **precipitation or rainfall**.
 
• The sun serves as the primary energy source, driving much of the evaporation observed on Earth. **Evaporation** typically occurs when water molecules on the surface of bodies of water become energized and ascend into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT correct regarding the food chain?

options.text: Every component of food chain forms trophic level.
Inter-relation between different food chains is known as a food web.
All the chains formed by nutritional relations are used to understand energy flow.
In food chain, energy level increases from lower trophic level to higher trophic level.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** In the food chain, the energy level increases from a lower trophic level to a higher trophic level.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A food chain **describes how energy and nutrients move through an ecosystem**.
 
• At the basic level, there are plants that produce the energy, then it moves up to** higher-level organisms like herbivores. **
 
• After that when carnivores eat the herbivores,** energy is transferred from one to the other.**
 
• There are** 2 types of food chains,** namely the **Grazing food chain and Detritus food chain**.
 
• Food chains are important because **they show the intricate relationships in ecosystems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82cb466a4599894653963420b2e47c7bdf9b4d3f590068430b38de9372e73d9c.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All of the interconnected and overlapping food chains in an ecosystem make up a food web.** Organisms in food chains are grouped into categories called** trophic levels.**
 
• The relationship between organisms is interlinked by a **food chain.** Food web: **It is the link between different food chains and presents what species eat in an ecological system**.
 
• **Energy flow** is the flow of energy through living things within an ecosystem.

questions.question:
In the context of ecology, the given equation shows the relationship between the size of an area and the number of species present in it. Accordingly, by which letter is the regression coefficient denoted?

log S = log C + Z log A
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Z.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** regression coefficient **in the given equation is denoted by the **letter Z.**
 
• The equation is known as the **species-area relationship** and is used to predict the number of species present in a given area based on its size.
 
• The coefficient Z represents the **slope of the regression line** and measures the **rate** at which the number of **species increases** with** increasing area.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** constant C** represents the intercept of the** regression line **and represents the** number of species** present in a unit area.
 
• **S** represents the** number of species.**
 
• **A** represents the **size of the area.**
 
• In general, there are more plant and animal species on** larger lands** than on smaller ones.
 
• Almost all terrestrial systems that have been investigated, from vast** continental regions** to **island archipelagos,** have shown this link to hold true.

questions.question: Which of the following nutrients is available mainly in apples?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**K.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium (K) **is the nutrient that is available mainly in** apples.**
 
• Apples are a good source of potassium, which is an essential mineral required for various bodily functions such as **heart health, nerve function, and muscle contraction.**
 
• Apples are also a good source of **fiber, vitamin C, and antioxidants** that can help promote overall health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cobalt **is required in trace amounts for the production of **vitamin B12** in the body.

 
 
• Vitamin B12, which aids in the synthesis of** red blood cells,** contains cobalt. 
 
 
 
• **Apples **are **low in sodium **and can be a good addition to a low-sodium diet.
 
 
• The body needs sodium, an essential nutrient, to keep **bodily fluids balanced** and to maintain **healthy muscles and neurons.**

questions.question: Water comes out of the leaves in the form of vapour by a process called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transpiration.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Water comes out of the leaves in the form of vapour by a process called** transpiration.**
 
• Transpiration is the process of **water movement through a plant** and its** evaporation from aerial parts, **mainly from the leaves but also from stems and flowers.
 
• During transpiration, water is pulled up from the roots through the** xylem vessels** by the process of **cohesion-tension, **which creates a **negative pressure gradient.**
 
• As water molecules evaporate from the **stomata (pores)** of the leaves, they create a suction force that helps to pull more water up from the roots, maintaining the **water flow.**
 
• Transpiration serves several functions for plants, including **cooling the leaves, providing water and nutrients to the cells,** and facilitating the **uptake of minerals from the soil.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Creepers:**

 
 
• Creepers are plants that **grow horizontally along the ground **or other surfaces, using specialized structures called adventitious roots to anchor themselves.
 
• Creepers** do not** have a direct role in water movement or transpiration.
 
 
 
• **Transportation:**
 
 
• In the context of plants, transportation can refer to the** movement of water, nutrients, and other substances **through the xylem and phloem tissues, but it is not specific to transpiration.
 
 
 
• **Venation:**
 
 
• Venation refers to the **pattern of veins or vascular tissues** in plant leaves, which can be either parallel or net-like.
 
• Venation is important for** plant growth and function, **but it is not directly related to transpiration.

• **Ecology** is the study of interactions between **living organisms **and their** environment.**
 
• It is a **branch of biology **that deals with the **study of organisms **and their** surroundings.**
 
• It encompasses a wide range of topics, including the **distribution and abundance of organisms,** the **functioning of ecosystems,** and the **impact of human activities **on the environment.
 
• Ecologists study the **relationships **between organisms and their environment at different levels, from individual organisms to entire ecosystems.
 
• The goal of ecology is to understand how organisms** interact with each other** and with their environment, and how these interactions** shape** the **structure and function of ecosystems.**

• Biosphere reserves are designated by **UNESCO **and typically include** core areas, buffer zones, and transition zones.**
 
 
 
• **Ecosystem**: An ecosystem is a **community of living organisms **and their **physical environment**, which includes both **biotic and abiotic factors.**
 
 
• **​**Ecosystems can range in size from** small ponds to entire biomes.**

• It was carried out in accordance with the **Indian Constitution's rules,** which were adopted on November 26, 1949.
 
• **1950** represents the year when the **Constitution** came into effect.

questions.question: Which of the following is an output of farming?

They help farmers to increase their efficiency and productivity, and reduce the labor required for manual tasks. Some common farm machines include tractors, harvesters, and irrigation systems.

questions.question: In which areas is intensive subsistence agriculture practiced?

options.text: area without population pressure on land

__
 
• **Gahana Nirvah Krishi** refers to intensive agriculture, where farmers use **advanced techniques **and **high-quality inputs** to maximize yields from a limited area of land.

• In areas with** high population pressure**, farmers practice intensive agriculture to produce **more food from limited land resources** to meet the increasing demand for food.

• In areas with** average population pressure**, farmers practice **semi-intensive agriculture,** which is a mix of intensive and extensive agriculture techniques.
 
• In areas with** no population pressure**, farmers may not practice agriculture at all, or they may practice **subsistence agriculture,** which is focused on producing enough food for their own consumption.

questions.question: What is the trophic level of dead organic matter in detritus food chain?

__
 
• The **detritus food chain** starts with the **dead organic matter, **which is then consumed by detritivores such as **earthworms, snails, and bacteria.**
 
• The dead organic matter is also known as** detritus,** and it is the** primary source of energy** for the detritus food chain.
 
• Since the dead organic matter is the** initial source of energy,** it is considered to be at the first trophic level.
 
• The detritus food chain is important as it helps in the** recycling of nutrients** in the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• These are usually **top predators** in the food chain.
 
 
 
• The **second trophic level **refers to the primary consumers, which are **herbivores.**
 
 
• They feed on **producers.**
 
 
 
• The** third trophic level **refers to the secondary consumers, which are **carnivores.**
 
 
• They feed on the** primary consumers.**

questions.question: Except for the deep sea hydrothermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. What comes next in the energy food chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **energy food chain **starts with the **sun**, which is the **primary source of energy** for all ecosystems on Earth.
 
• **Plants**, being the **primary producers,** are the next in the energy food chain.
 
• They use the sun's energy to produce food through** photosynthesis.**
 
• **Herbivores** come next in the chain, as they **consume plants **for their energy requirements.
 
• **Carnivores **come after herbivores, as they **consume other animals** for their energy requirements.
 
• Man is a** part** of the food chain, but not necessarily a next step.
 
• **Humans** can be herbivores or carnivores depending on their dietary habits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Herbivores** are animals that consume only plants as their **primary source of energy.**
 
• **Carnivores** are animals that consume other animals as their** primary source of energy.**
 
• **A food chain** is a straight line of living things that are eaten by other species to transfer **nutrients and energy.**
 
• Each organism in a food chain belongs to a distinct trophic level, which is determined by the number of energy transfers that separate it from the chain's fundamental input.

questions.question: Which of the following tiger reserves bagged the first ever international award 'TX2' in November for doubling the number of tigers in four years against the target of 10 years?

questions.question: Humus, a dark colored amorphous substance is formed as a result of which process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humification.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humus **is a dark-colored, amorphous substance that is** formed due to the process of humification.**

 
 
• **Humification **is the process by which dead organic matter, such as leaves, twigs, and other plant and animal remains, are broken down by microorganisms and transformed into humus.
 
 
 
• It is an important component of soil, as it improves soil fertility, water retention, and nutrient availability.
 
• It is **a complex mixture of organic compounds**, including **humic acids**,** fulvic acids**, and **humin**.
 
 
• **Humic acids** are the most abundant and important component of humus, and they play a key role in soil fertility by improving soil structure, nutrient availability, and water retention.
 
• **Fulvic acids** are smaller and more soluble than humic acids, and they are involved in the transport of nutrients and other substances within the soil.
 
• **Humin** is a highly stable component of humus that is resistant to further decomposition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragmentation **is the process by which large pieces of organic matter are broken down into smaller pieces, but it does not result in the formation of humus.
 
• **Leaching **is the process by which water carries dissolved nutrients and other substances from the soil surface to deeper layers, but it does not result in the formation of humus.
 
• **Mineralization **is the process by which microorganisms break down organic matter and release nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur into the soil to be easily available forms to plants.
